UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile and their general preferences within the VibeFlow application. Authentication details are handled externally.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: A public-facing username chosen by the user.

email.description: The user's email address, primarily for display and communication, not for authentication. (Security Best Practice: Do not store authentication credentials directly).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp of the user's last login.

preferredMediaFormat.description: The user's default preferred media format (e.g., Book, Series, Movie). This can be overridden per recommendation request.

preferredRealityType.description: The user's default preference for reality-based content (e.g., Fiction, Based on a Real Story). This can be overridden per recommendation request.

bio.description: An optional short biographical text provided by the user.

moodArchetypePreferenceIds.description: References to MoodArchetype entities that represent the user's generally preferred moods. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N MoodArchetype)

photoURL.description: URL of the user's profile picture.

subscriptionStatus.description: The user's subscription status, typically 'free' or 'pro'. Managed by the backend in a real application.

MoodArchetype.title: MoodArchetype
MoodArchetype.description: Defines a predefined emotional or thematic archetype that users can select to guide media recommendations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MoodArchetype entity.

name.description: The display name of the mood archetype (e.g., 'Adventure', 'Calm', 'Thoughtful').

description.description: A brief description explaining the essence of the mood archetype.

iconUrl.description: URL to an icon image representing this mood archetype.

MediaItem.title: MediaItem
MediaItem.description: Represents a single piece of media content, such as a book, movie, or series, available for recommendation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MediaItem entity.

title.description: The title of the media item.

authorCreator.description: The author for books, or creator/director for movies/series.

coverImageUrl.description: URL to the cover image of the media item.

synopsis.description: A brief summary or overview of the media item's plot or content.

realityType.description: Indicates if the media is fictional or based on a real story (e.g., 'Fiction', 'Based on a Real Story').

price.description: The standardized current price of the media item.

conclusionTakeaways.description: A list of tags or brief summaries describing the media item's core themes or emotional 'aftertaste' (e.g., 'Life-affirming', 'Bittersweet').

moodArchetypeIds.description: References to MoodArchetype entities that this media item is associated with or is likely to evoke. (Relationship: MoodArchetype N:N MediaItem)

averageRating.description: The denormalized average rating calculated from all user reviews for this media item.

RecommendationSession.title: RecommendationSession
RecommendationSession.description: Records a specific instance of a user requesting media recommendations, including their inputs and the list of media items suggested.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RecommendationSession entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who initiated this recommendation session. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N RecommendationSession)

selectedMoodId.description: Reference to the MoodArchetype selected by the user for this session. (Relationship: MoodArchetype 1:N RecommendationSession)

selectedFormat.description: The media format chosen by the user for this specific recommendation request.

selectedRealityType.description: The reality preference (Fiction/Based on a Real Story) chosen by the user for this specific recommendation request.

narrativeInput.description: The user's brief personal narrative or desired emotional outcome provided for this session.

timestamp.description: The date and time when this recommendation session was initiated.

recommendedMediaItemIds.description: An ordered list of references to MediaItem entities that were recommended to the user in this session. (Relationship: RecommendationSession 1:N MediaItem)

RecommendationDetail.title: RecommendationDetail
RecommendationDetail.description: Stores the specific 'why' explanation for a recommended media item within a particular recommendation session, as this explanation is dynamic and user-context specific.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RecommendationDetail entity.

recommendationSessionId.description: Reference to the RecommendationSession this detail belongs to. (Relationship: RecommendationSession 1:N RecommendationDetail)

mediaItemId.description: Reference to the MediaItem that was recommended. (Relationship: MediaItem 1:N RecommendationDetail)

recommendationWhy.description: The AI-generated or community-voted summary explaining why this specific media item matches the user's inputs for this session.

Review.title: Review
Review.description: Represents a user-submitted review and rating for a specific media item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Review entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who submitted this review. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Review)

mediaItemId.description: Reference to the MediaItem being reviewed. (Relationship: MediaItem 1:N Review)

rating.description: The star rating given by the user (e.g., 1-5).

reviewText.description: The detailed text content of the user's review.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the review was originally created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the review was last updated. Can be null if never updated.

RecommendationHistory.title: RecommendationHistory
RecommendationHistory.description: Represents a saved recommendation session for a user, including their inputs and the generated recommendations. This is a premium feature.

inputs.description: The inputs provided by the user for the recommendation.

outputs.description: The recommendations generated by the AI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the history item was created.

definition.description: Stores user profiles. The document ID (`userId`) MUST match the Firebase Authentication UID of the user. This path enables private, user-owned data.
Stores predefined mood archetypes. These are global, publicly readable, and managed by administrators.

params.name: moodId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific mood archetype.

definition.description: Stores all media content available for recommendations. These are global, publicly readable, and managed by administrators.

params.name: mediaItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific media item (book, series, movie).

definition.description: Stores a history of individual recommendation sessions for each user. The `userId` in the document MUST match the path's `userId`. This ensures user-specific access and Authorization Independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who initiated the recommendation session.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific recommendation session.

definition.description: Stores a user's recommendation history. Access is private to the user.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

params.name: historyId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific history entry.

definition.description: Stores the specific 'why' explanations for recommended media items within a recommendation session. `recommendationSessionId` in the document MUST match the path's `sessionId`. Authorization is inherited from the parent `RecommendationSession` through the path.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent recommendation session.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent recommendation session.

params.name: detailId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific recommendation detail.

definition.description: Stores user-submitted reviews and ratings for media items. Documents include denormalized `userId` (for ownership checks during writes) and `mediaItemId` (to match the parent path). This structure supports public reading of all reviews for a media item (QAP) and user-specific write access (Authorization Independence).

params.name: mediaItemId
params.description: The unique identifier of the media item being reviewed.

params.name: reviewId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific review.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for managing administrator roles. The document ID (`userId`) is the Firebase Authentication UID of an admin user. The existence of a document signifies admin status (DBAC).

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user designated as an administrator.

firestore.reasoning:
The VibeFlow Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and highly debuggable by strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence:** This is achieved primarily through structural segregation and strategic denormalization. For user-specific data like `UserProfile` and `RecommendationSession` (and its subcollection `RecommendationDetail`), a path-based ownership model is used: `/users/{userId}/...`. This ensures that the `userId` in the path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to a parent document for authorization. For `Review` documents, which are public-readable but user-writeable, they are placed under `/mediaItems/{mediaItemId}/reviews/{reviewId}`. To maintain authorization independence for write operations, the `userId` of the review's author is denormalized within the `Review` document itself, allowing rules to directly check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` without needing to fetch the user profile or any other parent data. Admin roles are managed via a dedicated top-level collection `/roles_admin/{userId}`, allowing for a simple `exists()` check rather than relying on custom claims or complex hierarchical data lookups.

**Queryable Access Patterns (QAPs):**

1.  **Publicly Accessible Data (e.g., browsing moods, media items):** Collections like `/moodArchetypes` and `/mediaItems` are top-level and have a uniform 'public read, admin write' security posture. This allows for efficient `list` operations (e.g., `db.collection('mediaItems').get()`) without security rules needing to filter results, as all documents are equally readable by anyone.
2.  **User-Specific Private Data (e.g., user profiles, recommendation history):** The `/users/{userId}` collection and its subcollections (`/users/{userId}/recommendationSessions`, `/users/{userId}/recommendationSessions/{sessionId}/recommendationDetails`) enforce strict ownership. `list` operations on these paths will inherently be constrained to the authenticated user's data, as the `userId` in the path matches `request.auth.uid`. This satisfies QAPs by ensuring that `list` queries within these paths only return data the user is authorized to see.
3.  **Mixed Access Data (e.g., reviews):** The `/mediaItems/{mediaItemId}/reviews` subcollection is designed for public `list` access (to view all reviews for a specific media item) while maintaining user-specific write access. A `list` query on `db.collection('mediaItems').doc(mediaItemId).collection('reviews')` will return all reviews for that media item, as they all share the 'public read' posture. Write access is then governed by the denormalized `userId` field within each `Review` document, ensuring only the author can modify their own review.

**Structural Segregation:** Each collection/subcollection (`users`, `moodArchetypes`, `mediaItems`, `recommendationSessions`, `recommendationDetails`, `reviews`, `roles_admin`) serves a distinct purpose and has a homogenous security posture, making rules simpler and easier to reason about.

**Access Modeling:** Path-based ownership is utilized for `UserProfile`, `RecommendationSession`, and `RecommendationDetail`. Global roles are handled by the `roles_admin` collection (Existence over Content). Collaborative data for `Review` entities is handled by public read access on the subcollection and denormalized `userId` for write access.

**Data Clarity:** Wildcards are descriptive (e.g., `{userId}`, `{mediaItemId}`). Authorization fields (`userId`, `recommendationSessionId`, `mediaItemId`) are explicitly present in documents where needed for security rules, making the intent clear. `createdAt` and `updatedAt` fields facilitate auditing and integrity checks. The overall structure prioritizes predictability and maintainability.
